source: Louvre stele, after R.F. Harper, The Code of Hammurabi, King of Babylon (Chicago, 1904): transliteration and autograph plates, List of Signs. Cuneiform in Old Babylonian monumental sign forms via the SantakkuM webfont by Sylvie Vanséveren (CC BY 4.0); pronunciation: conventional reconstructed Old Babylonian. Audio: a German synthetic voice reads the Akkadian word by word from these pronunciation rules (word stress after Huehnergard). about: Twenty-six laws on the people whose work can go wrong. The surgeon comes first (§215–223): a physician who opens a wound or the nagabtu (a word I cannot read, perhaps near the eye) and heals the man takes ten shekels from a man, five from a commoner, two from the owner of a slave (§215–217); if the patient dies, or loses his eye, the surgeon’s hands are cut off (§218), and for a commoner’s slave who dies he replaces the slave (§219). The animal doctor’s fees follow (§224–225), then the barber who shaves a slave’s mark off a slave that is not his: his hands are cut off, and the man who (as I read an unread verb) tricked him is killed and hanged at his gate (§226–227). The builder is next (§228–233): fee by the area built; and if the house falls and kills its owner the builder is killed, if it kills the owner’s son the builder’s son is killed, if a slave a slave, if goods the goods are replaced and the house rebuilt at his own cost. The last laws are the boatmen’s (§234–240): their fee for work on a boat (caulking, I think), their liability when a boat is sunk or its cargo lost, a boatman’s yearly hire, and a collision. Several words of the boat laws I cannot read and say so. Harper’s line numerals in col. xxxiv run one ahead of his own §-headings up to §221; I follow the running numerals. §239–240 are partly broken, and Harper’s square brackets are kept.

sentences.i: If a physician has made a severe wound in a man with a bronze knife,
sentences.n: Surgeons’ fees and penalties open here (§215–223: men and slaves; §224–225: animals; §226–227: the barber; §228–233: builders; §234–240: boatmen). Harper’s line numerals in col. xxxiv run one ahead of his own §-headings through §221; I follow the running numerals (they agree with the plate’s margin numbers 55, 60, 65 …). The usual šumma pattern: šumma asûm awīlam ṣimmam kabtam … īpušma, “if a physician has made a severe wound in a man …”. A.ZU is the two signs A and ZU with no ending; the case (asûm here) is the grammar’s. GÍR.NI is two signs I leave unread: some cutting tool (a knife); the exact kind I cannot say. siparrim “of bronze” is three signs, UD.KA.BAR, with no ending written (Harper’s list no. 148). ṣimmam: ZI read ṣi (Harper prints zi); “wound” is Harper’s sense, not derivable from the grammar (UNCERTAIN). kabtam “heavy, severe”. īpušma: i-bu-uš-ma, the sign BU read pu; preterite of epēšum “to do, make”, with -ma joining the next clause.

sentences.n: The owner of the sunk boat must prove his losses by oath: ina maḫar ilim ubârma “before the god he shall prove, and”, as in §126 (ubâršuma). tebiat, te-bi-a-at, is the stative (“is sunk”) of tebûm; ḫalqu “is lost” (ḫal-qu₂, the stative with the subjunctive -u; mimma is singular); GIŠ.MÁ-šu is said elippušu (Harper’s elippu-šu, the boat as subject) and elippišu (Harper’s elippi-šu, after ina); the case vowel is the grammar’s, not written. The first ša of line 72 is the relative “whose”.

sentences.n: ša maḫirtim ša … utebbû “the one of the maḫirtu who sank …”: utebbû with the subjunctive -u. iriabšum, i-ri-a-ab-šum: iriab “he shall replace” with -šum “for him” (the owner of the sunk boat). mimmâšu “his goods”, ḫalqam “lost” (Harper prints ḫal-ga-am with g; the sign is GA, read qa₂ as in earlier parts). glossary.epēšum: to do, make: epēšim “doing” · to work (land): ippeš(ma) (present): eqlam šipram ippeš “he shall do the work on the field” · to build (?) (a house): bītam ippēšma(?) “he builds a house, and”, the verb broken; iteppuš (?) in a broken line · ippešū (i-ib-bi-šu) “they shall do (work), they shall work” (present plural) · īpušu (i-pu-šu, preterite with the subjunctive -u) “(which) he built”: to make, build (a house) · ipuš (i-pu-uš, the sign BU read pu) “he made”: bīssu ipuš “he made his house”, i.e. set up a house of his own (preterite) · īpušma (i-bu-uš-ma, the sign BU read pu; preterite + -ma) “he made, and”: ṣimmam kabtam īpušma “he has made a severe wound”; bītam īpušma “he has built a house, and” · ippeš (i-ib-bi-eš, ibbi for ippi; present) “he shall rebuild”: bītam imqutu ippeš “he shall rebuild the house that fell”
glossary.eṣemtum: bone (written with the Sumerogram NER.PAD.DU, the three signs NER, PAD and DU, with no ending written): eṣemti (construct, before a genitive) “the bone of”, eṣemtašu “his bone” (with -šu, accusative); the Akkadian ending is supplied from the grammar, the exact form UNCERTAIN, the word is not · noun, Sumerogram
glossary.gallābum: barber (written with the Sumerogram ŠU.I, the two signs ŠU and I, with no ending written; from galābum “to shave”): gallābum (nominative), gallābim (genitive), gallābam (accusative); the endings are the grammar’s, not written · noun, Sumerogram
glossary.galābum-D: to shave (D-stem): ugallabū “they shall shave” · ugallib (u-gal-li-ib) “he has shaved off” and ugdallib (ug-da-al-li-ib, perfect) “he has shaved off”, of a barber and a slave-mark; ugallibu (u-gal-li-bu, first person with the subjunctive -u, in a quoted oath) “I shaved”: lā ugallibu “I did not shave”
glossary.idum: hire, wages (Harper: ID, the ideogram for hire): idi našpakim “the hire of the bin”, written with the single sign Á (A₂, “arm; hire”); the case ending is not written, so idi (construct, before a genitive) is an assumed reading, UNCERTAIN · idīšu (Á-šu, with -šu “his”) “his fee”, the physician’s pay: ana asîm idīšu “to the physician as his fee”; the case vowel is UNCERTAIN
glossary.idāṣ: UNCERTAIN: a verb I cannot read (the sign AZ read aṣ); the lemma is only the form idāṣ, and “to deceive” is the sense the law seems to need, not something the form shows: idāṣma (i-da-aṣ-ma, with -ma) “he has deceived (?), and” · verb, sense uncertain
glossary.igrum: hire, wages: ana igrim ittadin “he hired (him) out”
glossary.igārum: wall (written with the Sumerogram É.GAR₈, É and a second sign keyed GAR₃, the nearest sign in the sign glossary, so the key is UNCERTAIN; no ending written): igārum (nominative), igāram (accusative) “wall”; the endings are the grammar’s · noun, Sumerogram
glossary.ilum: god; here: the temple as owner · plural ilāni “gods” (written DINGIR.DINGIR, as in the litany): maḫar ilāni “before the gods”
glossary.ina: in, from · at (ina ebūrim “at harvest”); out of (ina bilat kirîm “out of the orchard’s yield”) · “through, by (means of)”: ina maḫāṣim “through beating”, ina pilšim “by a breach”; “regarding”: ina mimma ša … “regarding whatever …”; ina šanat “in the year”
glossary.ipḫi: UNCERTAIN: a verb I cannot read; “to caulk” (make watertight) is not shown by the form, only the sense a boatman’s fee for work on a boat seems to need; the lemma is only the form: ipḫi (ip-ḫi), ipḫima (ip-ḫi-ma, with -ma) “he has caulked (?)” · verb, sense uncertain
glossary.izzapar: UNCERTAIN: a verb I cannot read; it has the shape of an N-stem preterite (a present would be izzappar), but the root is not known; “is spoilt” is only the sense the next clause seems to need: izzapar (iz-za-par) · verb, sense uncertain
glossary.iṣēn: UNCERTAIN: a verb I cannot read; “to load” (a boat) is only the context’s sense, not shown by the form; the lemma is only the form: iṣēnši (i-ṣi-en-ši, with -ši “her”, the boat) “he has loaded her (?)” · verb, sense uncertain
glossary.kabtum: heavy; grave (of an offence): arnam kabtam (kab-tam, accusative) “a heavy offence” · of a wound, severe: ṣimmam kabtam (kab-tam, accusative) “a severe wound”
glossary.kalālum-Š: Š-stem (causative) of kalālum “to be complete”: to complete, finish: ušaklilšum (u-ša-ak-li-il-šum, with -šum “for him”) “he has completed (it) for him”, said of a house · Š-stem verb
glossary.kaspum: silver — the code’s money, written KÙ.BABBAR “shining precious-metal” · kaspim: mišil mana kaspim “half a mina of silver” · with a spelled vowel after the logogram: KÙ.BABBAR-a-am, -i-im, -u-um: kaspam, kaspim, kaspum (accusative, genitive, nominative); kaspum as the subject; the grain-and-silver pair šeʾam u kaspam “grain and silver” · kasap (KÙ.BABBAR, no ending written) construct “silver of”: kasap tirḫatim “silver of the bride-price”
glossary.kurrum: the kor, a grain measure (written GUR; Harper: 300 KA): kur šeʾam “a kor of grain” · written GUR.É (the editors’ print GUR-É) as well as GUR: 1 GUR.É, kurrum “a kor” (UNCERTAIN: the .É is not explained here) · written ŠE.GUR.E, with a final E: ana 1 ŠE.GUR.E “for one kor (of grain)”; the .E is not explained here, UNCERTAIN
glossary.kīma: like, as · as, like; with a verb in the subjunctive: kīma ubbalu “as he brings (it)” · according to: kīma ṣimdat šarrim “according to the king’s schedule” · “since, when”, before a stative: kīma mimmûšu lā ḫalqu “since his goods are not lost” · “in proportion to”: kīma emūq zittiša “in proportion to the strength of her share”, kīma emūq bīt abim “in proportion to the means of her father’s house”
glossary.leqûm: to take: ileqqi “he shall take” · ilqi “he took” (il-qi₂), ilqû (subjunctive, il-qu₂-u₂), ilqēma (il-qi₂-e-ma) “he took, and”, ilteqēma (perfect, il-te-qi₂-ma) “he has taken, and”; ša … ilqû “which he took” · ilqēma (il-qi₂-ma) “he took, and” (preterite ilqe + -ma, here without a spelled e); ilteqe (il-te-qi₂, perfect) “he has taken”; ileqqi (i-li-qi₂, present) “he shall take”; leqîm (li-qi₂-im, infinitive, genitive): ina kaspim leqîm “in the taking of the silver” · ileqqûma (i-li-qu₂-ma) “they shall take, and” (present plural + -ma); ileqqēma “he shall take, and” · ileqqû (i-li-qu₂-u) “they shall take” (present plural, without -ma) · ilqi (il-qi₂) “he took”; ilqûšu (il-qu₂-u-šu) “(when) he took him”, with the subjunctive -u and -šu “him”; ilqûšuma (il-qu₂-šu-ma) “he took him, and” (with the subjunctive -u before -šu, after ša); ana tarbītim ilqēma (il-qi₂-ma) “he took (him) as a foster-child, and”
glossary.libbum: heart · ana libbi “into”: ana libbi zittišu “into his share” · libbaša, libbiša (li-ib-ba-ša, li-ib-bi-ša) “her heart”: mala libbiša “as much as her heart wants”; libbaša uṭabbū “they shall make her heart good”, i.e. content her · ša libbiša (li-ib-bi-ša) “what is in her womb”, literally “that of her heart”, the unborn child: ana ša libbiša “for what was in her womb”
glossary.lā: not (in subordinate and nominal contexts) · before a noun in the genitive, “without”: lā kanīkim “without a sealed receipt”; in a šumma-clause, “not”: lā ītamar “he did not see”
glossary.lū: or; either (lū … lū “whether … or”); with verb: “let …”
glossary.makkūrum: property, assets — written with the Sumerogram Harper reads ŠA.GA (modern NÍG.GA)
glossary.malaḫum: boatman, sailor (written with the Sumerogram MÁ.DU.DU, the signs MÁ, DU and DU, i.e. MÁ.LAḪ₄; no ending written): malaḫum (nominative), malaḫim (genitive), malaḫam (accusative); the endings are the grammar’s · noun, Sumerogram
glossary.maqātum: to fall, collapse: imqutma (im-ku-ut-ma, preterite + -ma) “it has fallen, and” · imqutu (im-ku-tu, imqut with the subjunctive -u) “(which) fell”, “and it fell”: bītam imqutu “the house that fell” · verb
glossary.marṣum: sick, ill: marṣam (mar-ṣa-am, accusative) “sick”, agreeing with its noun · adjective
glossary.maḫar: before, in the presence of: maḫar ilim “before the god”
glossary.maḫirtum: UNCERTAIN: a kind of boat, sense unknown: maḫirtim (ma-ḫi-ir-tim, genitive; Harper restores part of the word in §240): ša maḫirtim “the one of the maḫirtu”, elippum ša maḫirtim “a boat of the maḫirtu” · noun, sense uncertain
glossary.maḫāṣum: to strike; of ground, to break up: imaḫḫaṣ “he shall break up” · the noun maḫāṣum “beating, abuse, injury” (Harper), written ma-ḫa-ṣi-im with the sign ZI (value ṣi): maḫāṣim “(through) beating” · imtaḫaṣ (im-ta-ḫa-aṣ, perfect) “he has struck”, imḫaṣma (preterite + -ma), amḫaṣ “I struck”: amḫassu (am-ḫa-zu) “I struck him” (ṣ + š said ss, written with ZU); the infinitive maḫāṣišu (ma-ḫa-zi-šu) “his striking, his blow”, ina maḫāṣišu “from his blow”
glossary.mimmûm: property, belongings: mimmûšu “his property” · mimmâšu (mi-im-ma-šu, accusative) “his goods”; mimmûšu (mi-im-mu-šu) “his goods” as subject; mimmê (mi-im-me-e, oblique): itti mimmê bēl bītim “with the goods of the owner of the house”; mimmēšu (mi-im-me-šu, oblique-looking, bracketed by Harper) “his goods”
glossary.mišlum: half: ana mišlāni “for halves” (in halves) · mišil (mi-ši-il) “half of”, before a noun: mišil šīmišu “half his price”, mišil šīmiša “half her price”
glossary.mukkelbītum: UNCERTAIN: a kind of boat, sense unknown: mukkelbītim (mu-uk-ki-el-bi-tim, genitive; Harper restores parts of the word in §240): elippam ša mukkelbītim “a boat of the mukkelbītu” · noun, sense uncertain
glossary.muškēnum: commoner, dependent freeman (MAŠ.EN.KAK) — the code’s second rank
glossary.mâtum-Š: Š-stem (causative) of mâtum “to die”: to make die, to kill: uštamīt (uš-ta-mi-it, perfect, 3rd singular) “he has caused (him) to die” · Š-stem verb
glossary.mārum: son (DUMU) — here: a minor, not yet able to sell · member of a group: mārū ugārim (DUMU A.GÀR{meš}) “the sons of the irrigated land”, the district’s farmers · mār awīlim “a man’s son” (DUMU); mārī (DUMU{meš}) “sons” (oblique plural, which may include daughters, so “children”); māršu (DUMU-šu) “his son” · mārūša (DUMU{meš}-ša) “her sons” (nominative plural + suffix); mārīša (DUMU-ša) “her son” (genitive + suffix): ana mārīša “to her son” · mārī (DUMU-i) “my son” (-ī “my”); mārī (DUMU{meš}) “children” in mārī ūlissum “children she bore him”; mārū (DUMU{meš}) “sons” as subject: mārū ana ummātim ul izuzzū “the sons shall not divide by mothers” · mār X (DUMU, the sign TUR) “a member of the class X”, literally “son of X”: mār ummiānim “a craftsman”, mār zinništim “the son of a woman”; māram (DUMU) “a son”, mārašu (DUMU-šu) “his son”, mārī (DUMU{meš}) “sons”, mārīšu “his sons”
glossary.nadānum: to give, pay: inaddin, iddinam, iddinušum; nadānim “to give” · iddin “he gave”; ana kaspim nadānum “to sell”: inaddinūma (present, plural) “they shall sell, and …” · iddin, iddinu “he gave” (preterite; the subjunctive -u in a ša- or inūma clause); iddinma “he gave, and”; …in, …din in broken forms; inaddin “he shall give”: ana damqaršu inaddin “he shall give to his merchant” · ittadinma (it-ta-di-in-ma) “he has given, and” (perfect); inaddinu (i-na-ad-di-nu) “(which) he gives” (present, with the subjunctive -u) · ittandin (it-ta-an-di-in, perfect with an extra -n-) “he has handed over”: ana kiššātim ittandin “he handed over into service”; ittadin (it-ta-din) “he has given”, i.e. sold; ana maṣṣarūtim inaddin “he gives for safekeeping”; iddinūšumma “they gave him, and” · inaddin also of a woman, “she shall give” · inaddišši (i-na-ad-di-iš-ši) “he/she shall give her” (the n of the stem swallowed before -ši), of a sale: ana kaspim inaddišši “she may sell her”, ul inaddišši “she shall not sell her” · anaddin “I shall give”, with the n merged into the k of -kum: anaddikkum (a-na-ad-di-ik-kum) “I shall give (her) to you”; iddinu (id-di-nu) “(which) he gave”; iddinušum “he gave him” · nadānam (na-da-nam, infinitive accusative) “to give”: warkassa … nadānam “(that she may) give her estate” · iddišši (id-di-iš-ši) “he gave her”, preterite + -ši, the n written š: ana mutim iddišši “he gave her to a husband” · inaddinūši (i-na-ad-di-nu-ši) “they shall give her”, inaddinūšimma (i-na-ad-di-nu-šim-ma) “they shall give her, and”, ittadnūšimma (it-ta-ad-nu-ši-im-ma) “they have given her, and” (perfect plural + -šim + -ma) · iddinušim (id-di-nu-ši-im) “he gave her”, with the subjunctive -u in a ša-clause
glossary.nagabtum: UNCERTAIN: a word I cannot read (Harper’s na-gab-ti); the context suggests a part of or near the eye, but the meaning is not secure, and neither is the exact form: nagabti (na-gab-ti, before a genitive: “the nagabtu of …”), nagabtašu (na-gab-ta-šu) “his nagabtu”, with -šu · noun, sense uncertain
glossary.nakāsum: to cut, cut down: ikkis (preterite) “he cut down” · inakkisū (i-na-ak-ki-su) “they shall cut off”, present plural (the ending -sū is written with the one sign su, as Harper prints it): lišānšu inakkisū “they shall cut off his tongue”, tulêša inakkisū “they shall cut off her breast” · inakkisū “they shall cut off”, of the hand(s) and the ear: rittēšu inakkisū “they shall cut off his hand(s)”, uznašu inakkisū “they shall cut off his ear”
glossary.naqārum: UNCERTAIN: to tear down, demolish, from the sense of the clause: inaqqarma (i-na-qar-ma, the sign GAR read qar; present + -ma) “he shall tear down, and” · verb, sense uncertain
glossary.petûm: to open; of land, to bring into cultivation: iptete “he has opened” · preterite ipte, iptēma “he opened” · iptēma (ip-te-ma) “he has opened, and”, of a part of the body, with a knife
glossary.qatāpum: UNCERTAIN: iqtup (iq-tu-up) has the shape of a preterite of qatāpum; “has given way” (of a wall) is only the sense the context seems to need, not something the form shows · verb, sense uncertain
glossary.qīštum: gift: qīšti šarrum ana rēdîm iddinu “the gift the king gave the soldier”
glossary.ramānum: self: ramānšu ipaddar “he shall redeem himself”
glossary.rašûm: to get, acquire: irtaši “he has acquired”, iraššû “he acquires” · iršû (ir-šu-u) “(whom) he has acquired” (the relative -u): ana mārī ša iršû “for the sons whom he has acquired”
glossary.rebûm: fourth: rebûtim šattim “in the fourth year” · rebūt (IGI.4.GAL) “one quarter”: rebūt šīmišu “a quarter of its price”; the spoken form is reconstructed, UNCERTAIN
glossary.rittum: hand: rittēšu (UM.ME-šu, the signs UM, ME and ŠU) “his hand(s)”, with -šu “his”; Harper normalizes rit-tê-šu with an ending -ê whose grammar is not clear to me; the second sign (read ME) and the number, one hand or two, are both UNCERTAIN · noun
glossary.siparrum: bronze (written with the Sumerogram UD.KA.BAR, the three signs UD, KA and BAR, with no ending written): siparrim (genitive) “of bronze”; the case ending is the grammar’s, not written · noun, Sumerogram
glossary.suluppum: dates (written with the Sumerogram ZÚ.LUM, the signs KA and LUM): suluppam (accusative); the ending is the grammar’s, not written · noun, Sumerogram
glossary.takālum-D: UNCERTAIN: the D-stem of takālum “to trust”, taken as “to make trustworthy, reliable” from the meaning of the stem, not from the context: utakkilma (u-tak-ki-il-ma, with -ma): lā utakkilma “he has not made (it) reliable (?), and” · D-stem verb, sense uncertain
glossary.tamûm: to swear (an oath): itamma (i-tam-ma, present, 3rd singular) “he shall swear”, itammama (i-tam-ma-ma) “he shall swear, and”, with -ma · verb
glossary.tebûm: to rise; Š-stem: ušetbûšuma “they shall make him rise (be removed)” · stative tebiat (te-bi-a-at) “is sunk”, said of a boat: elippišu tebiat “his boat is sunk”; here the sense is “sink”, not “rise”, and it is taken from the law, UNCERTAIN; the D-stem “to sink” (transitive) is entered as tebûm-D
glossary.tebûm-D: UNCERTAIN: D-stem of tebûm, here “to sink” (transitive: to sink a boat), a sense taken from the stem and the law, not shown by the form; the opposite of uštēliašši “he has raised her” (see elûm-Š): uttebbi (ut-te-bi, ut-te-ib-bi, perfect) “he has sunk (it)”; utebbima (u-te-ib-bi-ma, preterite + -ma) “he sank, and”; utebbû (u-te-ib-bu-u, with the subjunctive -u) “(which) he sank”: elippam ša utebbû “the boat that he sank” · D-stem verb, sense uncertain
glossary.uštēṣbi: UNCERTAIN: a Š-stem perfect of a root I do not know; “to make right, true” is only a guess from the context: uštēṣbima (uš-te-iṣ-bi-ma, with -ma) “he has made (it) right (?), and”; the lemma is only the form · Š-stem verb, sense uncertain
glossary.wardum: male slave (ARAD) · warad (ARAD, no ending written) “male slave of …”, wardam (ARAD-am)
glossary.wašārum: D-stem (w)uššurum “to release, set free”: ūtaššar “he shall be released” · the form ūtaššar (ū-ta-aš-šar) is the Dt, the t-form of the D-stem, in the present: “he shall be released”; the “D-stem” named above is the stem family, and this form is its t-form (Dt)
glossary.īnum: eye: īnšu … iššīma “he lifted his eye (to it)” — he coveted it · ša īnšu maḫru (i-in-šu) “whose eye is first” = the son he favours (UNCERTAIN idiom)
glossary.šalāmum-Š: Š-stem (causative) of šalāmum “to be whole, sound”: to make whole, to heal: uštalim (uš-ta-li-im, perfect, 3rd singular) “he has made (it) whole”, said of a broken bone · Š-stem verb
glossary.šamnum: oil, fat (written Ì.GIŠ, the signs NI + GIŠ): šamnam (accusative; Harper šamnu)
glossary.šaqālum: to weigh out (silver = to pay): išqulu · išaqqal (present) “he shall weigh out”
glossary.šattum: year: šattam (syllabic, §31) or MU (the year-sign, §30) · šattim (genitive); plural šanātim “years” (ša šanātim “of the years”); MU 4{kam}, said erbe šanātim “four years” · MU 3{kam}, said šalāš šanātim “for three years”; šanat (ša-na-at) “(in) the year”, ina šanat “each year”
glossary.šebirtum: break, fracture (Harper’s sense; from šebērum “to break”): šebirtam (še-bi-ir-tam, accusative) “a broken (part)”, said of a bone · noun
glossary.šerʾānum: UNCERTAIN: a body part, perhaps “sinew, muscle”, a guess from the sound and from the sense (something that can be sick and be healed): šerʾānam (še-ir-ḫa-nam, the ʾ written with the sign ḪA, accusative) “a sinew (?)”; Harper prints the spelling as two words, še-ir ḫa-nam · noun, sense uncertain
glossary.šeʾum: barley, grain (the ŠE sign) · ŠE-am, ŠE-im, ŠE-um, written with the logogram and a spelled vowel; šeʾum as the subject; ŠE-am-ma “grain only” (with the restricting -ma); in broken forms še…
glossary.šipru: work, task, workmanship: šipiršu (ši-bi-ir-šu, the sign BI for pi, with -šu “his”) “his work”: šipiršu lā udanninma “he has not made his work strong” · noun
glossary.šipātum: wool (written SIG, as Harper’s glossary gives it): šipâtam (accusative; Harper šipâtu)
glossary.šiqlum: shekel — the basic weight of silver, about 8.3 g (written GÍN): 2 šiqil kaspim
glossary.šumma: if — the word that opens every law of the code
glossary.šuāti: that, the aforesaid · as the independent pronoun “him”: šuāti u bīšašu “him and his goods”
glossary.šuššum: one-sixth (written IGI.6.GAL, “the sixth part”): šuššum “a sixth”; in the silver rate it is followed by 6 še, “one-sixth and 6 grains” (IGI.6.GAL šeššet šeʾam) · šuššat (IGI.6.GAL, before kaspim) “one sixth”, of a shekel of silver; the unit is not written, and the spoken form is reconstructed, UNCERTAIN
glossary.šû: UNCERTAIN: lā šēm (la še-e-im, the signs ŠE, E and IM) in “a slave not his”, read as a form of the pronoun šû “he, his”, from the context and not from the form: wardi lā šēm “of a slave who is not his” · pronoun, form uncertain
glossary.šī: she, that (feminine pronoun, as the independent word): ŠAL.GEŠ.TIN.NA šī “that tavern-keeper”; the masculine is šū
glossary.šīmum: purchase, purchase price · šīmišu (ŠÁM-šu, with -šu “his”) “his price”, of a slave: mišil šīmišu “half of his price” · šīmiša (ŠÁM-ša, with -ša “her”) “her price”, of a boat: mišil šīmiša “half her price”; šīmišu “its price”, of an animal: rebūt šīmišu “a quarter of its price”
glossary.ḫabātum-D: UNCERTAIN verb, the D-stem (intensive) of ḫabātum “to rob, plunder”, taken here as “to destroy” from the sense of the law, not from the grammar: uḫtabbit (uḫ-tab-bi-it, perfect, 3rd singular) “he has destroyed (?)”, said of an eye · D-stem verb, sense uncertain
glossary.ḫalālum: to hang up: iḫallalūšu “they shall hang him” (in the breach he cut) · iḫallalūšu (i-ḫa-al-la-lu-šu) “they shall hang him”, at his gate: ina bābīšu iḫallalūšu; “hang” is the usual sense of the verb, not shown by the form, UNCERTAIN
glossary.ḫalāqum: to be lost, vanish: ḫalqu, ḫalqam · iḫtaliq (iḫ-ta-li-iq, perfect) “it has been lost”; ḫaliq (ḫa-li-iq, stative) “(it) is lost”, ḫaliqma “is lost, and”; lā ḫaliqma “is not lost, and”
glossary.ḫalāqum-D: D-stem of ḫalāqum “to be lost, to perish”: to destroy, cause to be lost: uḫalliqu (preterite, with the relative -u) “(the grain) he destroyed” · uḫtalliq (uḫ-ta-al-li-iq, perfect, 3rd singular) “he has destroyed”: šumma makkūr uḫtalliq “if he has destroyed property”; of a boatman, ù lū uḫtalliq “or has destroyed (it)”
glossary.ḫiṭītum: UNCERTAIN: sin, fault, defect: ḫiṭītam (ḫi-ṭi-tam, accusative); Harper prints ḫi-di-tam, but the middle sign DI also reads ṭi, and his glossary does not list the word, so the identification rests on the sign reading and the context
glossary.ṣimmum: wound (Harper’s sense), UNCERTAIN, not derivable from the grammar: ṣimmam (ṣi-im-ma-am, accusative) “a wound”; the first sign is the sign ZI in the autograph (Harper prints zi-im-ma-am here), read ṣi · noun, sense uncertain
glossary.ṣīnum: UNCERTAIN: a word I cannot read with certainty (ṣi-nim, genitive), in the phrase mimma šumšu ša ṣīnim “anything whatever of ṣīnum”, after the goods loaded on a boat; “cargo” is only the sense the context suggests · noun, sense uncertain
